questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to implement tenant-isolated behavior using sidecar patterns and ConfigMap-driven configuration, ensuring no cross-tenant impact while maintaining per-tenant control over canary deployment parameters.

## Key Concepts

- Namespace-scoped configuration through ConfigMap volume mounting
- Lightweight per-tenant canary routing implementation
- Traffic management via sidecar proxy pattern
- JSON-based configuration parsing and validation
- Percentage-based traffic distribution algorithms

## Code Example

```yaml
# Canary configuration ConfigMap
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: canary-config
  namespace: tenant-1
data:
  canary.json: |
    {"percent":20,"enabled":true}
---
# Sidecar deployment with ConfigMap mount
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: canary-sidecar
  namespace: tenant-1
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: canary-sidecar
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: canary-sidecar
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: sidecar
        image: canary-router:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: canary-config
          mountPath: /etc/cnf
      volumes:
      - name: canary-config
        configMap:
          name: canary-config
```

Why This Is Asked

- Exercises understanding of the sidecar pattern, process supervision, and per-tenant isolation.
- Checks how backoff, crash loops, and health endpoints are wired in Kubernetes.

Key Concepts
- Process supervision and exit handling in a container.
- Per-tenant state via labels/annotations and isolated metrics.
- Liveness/readiness semantics and crash-loop protection.

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  labels:
    app: cnf-gateway
    tenant: <tenant-id>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cnf-gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cnf-gateway
        tenant: <tenant-id>
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: cnf-main
          image: cnf/main:latest
        - name: watchdog
          image: cnf/watchdog:latest
          env:
            - name: CNF_MAIN_BIN
              value: "/cnf/main/bin/cnf"
          volumeMounts:
            - mountPath: "/cnf/main/bin"
              name: bin
      volumes:
        - name: bin
          emptyDir: {}
```

Tests practical ability to implement per-tenant mTLS for CNF gateways using Kubernetes CSR flow and secret management without a global PKI.

## Key Concepts

- Kubernetes CertificateSigningRequest flow
- Per-namespace per-tenant CA
- Secret volumes and TLS configuration in a sidecar
- TLS handshake verification with control plane

## Code Example

```yaml
# CSR manifest (example)
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: gateway-client-tenant-a
spec:
  groups:
  - system:authenticated
  request: <base64 CSR>
  usages:
  - digital signature
  - key encipherment
  - client auth
```

```yaml
# Secret CA manifest (example)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-ca
  namespace: tenant-a
type: Opaque
data:
  ca.crt: <base64-encoded CA cert>
```

```yaml
# Test manifest (gateway pod)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gateway-test
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  containers:
  - name: gateway
    image: cnf/gateway:latest
    volumeMounts:
    - name: tls
      mountPath: /etc/certs
  volumes:
  - name: tls
    secret:
      secretName: tenant-a-gateway-client-cert
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you rotate per-tenant certificates without downtime?
- How would you validate client cert revocation in the control plane?
